entries.text:
Jacobs’s Concerto Köln Giulio Cesare is the Italian-language HIP studio classic for this opera: Larmore’s Cesare fearless in the runs, Schlick’s Cleopatra sharp in colour, Fink and Rørholm binding Cornelia and Sesto. Concerto Köln answers the score’s obbligatos and double orchestra with dramatic bite. Against the Baker/Mackerras ENO set in English it is the other language and the other instrumentarium — complete Italian studio drama rather than English theatre document.

Some tempi sit slower than habit; a few rallentandos jar. The set still leads the Italian complete argument on disc. Harmonia Mundi’s four-CD face is the object — not excerpts.

entries.text:
Baker’s Julius Caesar for Mackerras and the ENO is the English-language modern-instrument document that still matters: sovereign Handelian mezzo, Masterson’s Cleopatra touching, Bowman and Tomlinson vivid in the court. Mackerras paces recitative and aria with theatre sense; the Abbey Road studio set preserves an ENO generation at full strength.

Against Jacobs’s Italian HIP complete it is another work in another tongue — cuts exist, period instruments do not. The later Chandos reissue carries the same 1984 Abbey Road tapes, not a remake. Keep it for Baker and for the English theatre pole of the Cesare argument.
